stem: On a number line, points A, B and C are such that \(d(A, B) = 5\), \(d(B, C) = 11\) and \(d(A, C) = 6\). Which of the points is between the other two?
solution:
Which of the points A, B and C is between the other two, can be decided as follows.
\(d(B, C) = 11\) .... (I)
\(d(A, B) + d(A, C) = 5 + 6 = 11\) .... (II)
\(\therefore d(B, C) = d(A, B) + d(A, C)\) .... [from (I) and (II)]
Point A is between point B and point C.
diagramNote: Fig. 1.3 shows a number line with B, A, C in that order, the gap B to A marked 5 and the gap A to C marked 6.

stem: U, V and A are three cities on a straight road. The distance between U and A is 215 km, between V and A is 140 km and between U and V is 75 km. Which of them is between the other two?
solution:
\(d(U, A) = 215\); \(d(V, A) = 140\); \(d(U, V) = 75\)
\(d(U, V) + d(V, A) = 75 + 140 = 215\); \(d(U, A) = 215\)
\(\therefore d(U, A) = d(U, V) + d(V, A)\)
\(\therefore\) The city V is between the cities U and A.

stem: The co-ordinate of point A on a number line is 5. Find the co-ordinates of points on the same number line which are 13 units away from A.
solution:
As shown in the figure, let us take points T and D to the left and right of A respectively, at a distance of 13 units.
The co-ordinate of point T, which is to the left of A, will be \(5 - 13 = -8\)
The co-ordinate of point D, which is to the right of A, will be \(5 + 13 = 18\)
\(\therefore\) the co-ordinates of points 13 units away from A will be \(-8\) and \(18\).
Verify your answer : \(d(A, D) = d(A, T) = 13\)
diagramNote: Fig. 1.4 shows a number line with T at \(-8\), A at 5 and D at 18, with arcs marked \(5-13\) from A to T and \(5+13\) from A to D.

stem:
Theorem : The opposite angles formed by two intersecting lines are of equal measures.

Line AB and line CD intersect at point O such that A - O - B, C - O - D. Prove that (i) \(\angle AOC = \angle BOD\) (ii) \(\angle BOC = \angle AOD\).
solution:
Given : Line AB and line CD intersect at point O such that A - O - B, C - O - D.

To prove : (i) \(\angle AOC = \angle BOD\)
(ii) \(\angle BOC = \angle AOD\)

Proof :
\(\angle AOC + \angle BOC = 180^\circ\) ....... (I)   (angles in linear pair)
\(\angle BOC + \angle BOD = 180^\circ\) ....... (II)   (angles in linear pair)
\(\angle AOC + \angle BOC = \angle BOC + \angle BOD\) ....... [from (I) and (II)]
\(\therefore \angle AOC = \angle BOD\) ...... eliminating \(\angle BOC\).

Similarly, it can be proved that \(\angle BOC = \angle AOD\).
diagramNote: Fig. 1.15 — line AB and line CD crossing at O; going anticlockwise round O the rays are A, C, B, D so that A-O-B and C-O-D are straight lines.

stem: Statement : A prime number greater than 2 is odd. Write this statement in conditional form and prove it by an indirect proof.
solution:
Conditional statement : If \(p\) is a prime number greater than 2 then it is odd.

Given : \(p\) is a prime number greater than 2. That is, 1 and \(p\) are the only divisors of \(p\).

To prove : \(p\) is an odd number.

Proof : Let us suppose that \(p\) is not an odd number.
So \(p\) is an even number.
\(\therefore\) a divisor of \(p\) is 2 ..... (I)
But it is given that \(p\) is a prime number greater than 2.   ....(given)
\(\therefore\) 1 and \(p\) are the only divisors of \(p\) ..... (II)
Statements (I) and (II) are contradictory.
\(\therefore\) the assumption, that \(p\) is not odd is false.
This proves that a prime number greater than 2 is odd.
